html:
A poet of Florence, author of the Divine Comedy, the greatest poem of the Middle Ages. He was born in 1265 into a family of minor nobility.

As a young man he fell in love with Beatrice Portinari, whom he barely knew and who died in 1290; she became the guiding figure of his poetry, as told in his early book La Vita Nuova. He fought at the battle of Campaldino and went into politics in Florence, a city split between rival factions. In 1302, while he was away on a mission to Pope Boniface VIII, his enemies took over and sentenced him to exile, and later to death if he came back.

He never returned. He moved between Italian courts and wrote the Comedy in exile, finishing it shortly before he died at Ravenna in 1321. He wrote it not in Latin but in the Tuscan dialect, so that ordinary readers could follow it. His guide through Hell in the poem is the Roman poet Virgil. With Petrarch and Boccaccio, he made Tuscan the basis of written Italian.
